_readme: The MiMo Code wire values that both the Go provider and the TypeScript plugin spell. MiMo runs as `mimo serve`, a local HTTP server with a server-sent event stream; the worker reads that stream and persists some of its events verbatim, so the browser plugin dispatches on the same words. `events` holds only the event types the worker persists and the browser reads: a tool part as `message.part.updated`, the turn end as `session.status`, a turn failure as `session.error`, and the stored payload of a permission request as `permission.asked`. The other event types (message deltas, the actor, task, goal, workflow and inbox events) stay in the Go provider, because the browser never receives them. A question and its answer envelope use the OpenCode vocabulary in `opencode-protocol.json`, because MiMo sends the same shapes. `statusTypes` holds the `status.type` words of `session.status`. `partTypes` holds the part `type` words the browser draws; the text and reasoning parts become assembled messages in the worker and stay in Go. `toolStatuses` holds the `state.status` words of a tool part. `toolNames` holds the tool ids: on MiMo, `task` is the work-item tracker and `actor` starts a subagent, which is the opposite of upstream OpenCode. `actorActions`, `taskActions` and `taskStatuses` are the operation and status words those two tools carry. `modes` holds the primary agents LeapMux states itself, which LeapMux carries on its permission-mode axis so that plan mode and plan approval work as they do for every provider; the server may offer more agents, and `defaultMode` is the one a new session runs. `options` and `permissionPolicies` are LeapMux's own: MiMo has no permission-mode enumeration, so LeapMux offers one axis whose three values each set MiMo's two runtime switches, skip-all and auto-approve-delete. `permissionReplies` holds the answers a permission reply carries. `controlFields` holds the field that LeapMux adds to a stored plan-approval payload. `actorStatuses` and `actorOutcomes` hold the words of a subagent (an actor): its status, and the outcome of its last turn, which `actor wait` and `actor status` state as `lastOutcome`.

Pending.why: the worker opens and closes a subagent row on `running` and `idle` alone, because MiMo publishes only those two in `actor.status`; the browser reads the other words from the result of an `actor wait` or `actor status` call
